# 6 Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion

- [weak] "Pragmatism may be a happy harmonizer…": The quote is lowercase "pragmatism may be…" from "the claim I made… that pragmatism may be…". The statement drops the "claim" framing but is supported as a hedged claim.
- [dangling] "Men who are strongly of the fact-loving temperament are liable to be kept at a distance by the small sympathy with facts which that philosophy from the present-day fashion of idealism offers them.": "that philosophy from the present-day fashion of idealism" is OK, but the statement is not tied to pragmatism or the claim in a way the reader can resolve. Minor. Pass on reference; the cut is fine.
- [dangling] "It is far too intellectualistic.": "It" could refer to idealism or the philosophy. Reasonably resolvable from the prior statement ("that philosophy"). Borderline pass.
- [dangling] "But, the brand of pantheism offered is hard for them to assimilate…": "them" refers to the fact-loving men, resolvable. The "But," joins to the previous statement about pantheism. The cut dropped "as I said in my first lecture", which is how-the-author-knows, so it is fine. Pass.
- [dangling] "It is the absolutistic brand…" / "It keeps no connexion…": "It" is resolvable to the brand of pantheism. Pass.
- [dangling] "Be they what they may, the Absolute will father them.": "them" is resolvable to particulars of fact. Pass.
- [dangling] "But from the human point of view, no one can pretend that it doesn't suffer from the faults of remoteness and abstractness.": "it" has the Absolute and pantheism as candidates, and the source says "this conception", which refers to the Absolute. Resolvable but loose. The cut dropped "Far be it from me to deny the majesty of this conception… But", and the "But" concedes a point whose content is lost. This is cut lost content, a minor case.
- [cut lost content] "It is eminently a product of the rationalistic temper.": Spliced from "what I have ventured to call the rationalistic temper". The trimmed words are the author's framing only, so this passes. The splice itself is fine.
- [dangling] "In this real world of sweat and dirt, when a view of things is 'noble,'…": The cut dropped "it seems to me that". This is stance only, so it passes.
- [dangling] "His menial services are needed in the dust of our human trials…": "His" refers to "the God of earth and heaven" in the previous statement. Pass.
- [dangling] "Now pragmatism, devoted tho she be to facts…": "ordinary empiricism" is not introduced earlier in this note, though "empiricist ways of thinking" is. Pass.
- [dangling] "What I, William James, said just now about the Absolute of transcendental idealism is a case in point.": "just now" and "transcendental idealism" point to earlier statements, which are present in the note. The name span is addressed below. Pass.
- [dangling] "First, I called it majestic and said it yielded religious comfort…": The "majestic" claim is not in this note, because the "Far be it from me…" sentence was omitted. The statement is supported by its quote, but "it" and the claim refer to content absent from the note. Dangling on "it", which is resolvable only as the Absolute.
- [dangling] "The universe is a system of which the individual members may relax…": "his being true" and "his cash-value" refer to the Absolute, which was named before. Pass.
- [dangling] "He can use the Absolute for so much…": "He" is resolvable to the "ordinary lay-reader". Pass.
- [dangling] "He is pained at hearing you speak incredulously…": "you" here is the lecturer's hypothetical critic, which is generic. Pass.
- [dangling] "If the Absolute means this, and means no more than this…": "this" is resolvable to the preceding moral-holiday statements. Pass.
- [dangling] "I am well aware how odd it must seem to some of you to hear me say…": "me" is named by the earlier name span "William James" in this note. Pass.
- [dangling] "That it is GOOD, for as much as it profits, you will gladly admit.": "it" refers to the idea, which is resolvable from the previous statement. Pass.

Counts: pass 41 / weak 1 / fail 0 / dangling 2 / outside-frame 0, plus cut lost content 1.
